title: Reuters ownership and control
summary: Reuters is a British international news agency within Canada’s Thomson Reuters Corporation. Woodbridge and its affiliates held approximately 71% of Thomson Reuters’ common shares as of June 30, 2026. The Founders Share Company holds separate protective rights. Research conducted for September 17, 2026; findings are unreviewed.

nodes.name: Reuters
nodes.description: British international news agency and news service, with its UK editorial headquarters in London and operations worldwide.
nodes.endpointNote: Identified as the Reuters news business within Thomson Reuters.

nodes.name: Thomson Reuters Corporation
nodes.description: Canadian publicly traded information and technology company whose businesses include Reuters.
nodes.endpointNote: Ownership and special protective control rights are traced separately.

nodes.name: The Woodbridge Company Limited
nodes.description: Private Thomson family investment company. The reported 71% interest includes affiliated companies, rather than Woodbridge alone.
nodes.endpointNote: Followed to its disclosed holding company, Thomson Investments Limited.

nodes.name: Thomson Investments Limited
nodes.description: Holding company of Woodbridge involved in the Thomson family’s ownership arrangements.
nodes.endpointNote: Third relationship level reached. The filings identify the 2003 TIL Settlement as holding the relevant holding-company shares; that additional relationship is beyond the graph’s depth limit.

nodes.name: Other Thomson Reuters common shareholders
nodes.description: Aggregate common-share interests outside Woodbridge and its affiliates; approximately 29% by subtraction from the reported rounded 71% holding.
nodes.endpointNote: Remainder is aggregated, not an identified single owner. Individual positions were not established.

nodes.name: Thomson Reuters Founders Share Company Limited
nodes.description: Corporate guardian of the Trust Principles, with special voting and transaction-consent rights.
nodes.endpointNote: Protective rights are verified. Its trustees are selected through a nomination committee and appointed by its board; ultimate legal membership or ownership was not established.

edges.description: The company identifies Reuters as part of Thomson Reuters. This represents the news business’s corporate parent, without asserting an unverified intermediate legal-entity chain.

edges.description: Limited protective control: special voting rights apply in specified acquisition or significant-shareholding circumstances. This is not ordinary management control or an economic ownership percentage.
The Founders Share Company’s prior consent is required for a sale or other material transaction involving the Reuters news business.

evidence.title: The Trust Principles
evidence.excerpt: any sale of, or other material transaction involving, the Reuters news business unit

gaps: Recent-sale searches found no supported transfer of the Reuters news business. The July 2026 announced KKR transaction concerns Global Print, a separate business.
June 30, 2026 is the latest verified ownership observation used here. Subsequent share transactions or repurchases may change the rounded percentages.
Reuters is represented as the news agency and business, rather than as a particular national publishing subsidiary; the complete intermediate legal-entity structure was not verified.
The three-level limit stops the corporate chain at Thomson Investments Limited. Filings describe the 2003 TIL Settlement, its Thomson family beneficiaries and trustee arrangements beyond that point.
Family members’ individual economic interests and the composition of the public-shareholder remainder were not established.
The official Trust Principles page is undated, so dates for its protective-rights observations are null.
